reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 argument-2 of MOD must not be zero; a reference whose argument-2 is zero at the time of reference has an undefined result (§1989:A.2.2), so the compiler must evaluate every nonzero divisor correctly (literal, item, computed, negative) and may do anything for a zero divisor.

edition-consulted.switches: ArgumentFunctionChecking (set only by a >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION statement guard); no TURN directive exists at 85, so the flag stays off and the default result 0 is returned

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior over CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs, CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs and the MOD arms of IntrinsicRenderer.cs: none; the only switch is the runtime checking flag, which is the default (off) arm at every edition unless TURN is written
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: a zero divisor yields 0 at 85 and at 2023 (2023 adds EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION under checking, which 85 lacks)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf41_01 keeps argument-2 nonzero (literal, negative literal, computed divisor); no witness runs a zero divisor, which the rule leaves undefined

probes.expected: undefined result (§1989:A.2.2); no diagnostic required for literal 0

probes.expected: undefined result for item 0, computed 0 (D3 - 3) and ZERO; execution may continue

probes.expected: §1989:A.2.28.4 RV1 floored modulus for nonzero divisors

OK  §1989:A.2.2  (2.2 ARGUMENTS**)  the text is in the clause; it lies in AR4 [do not have values within the permissible range, then the result of such a reference is undefined]

reader.notes: The 1985 text makes a zero argument-2 an out-of-range value whose reference result is undefined, so the compiler's 0 with continued execution is a permitted result; nonzero divisors of every shape probed are exact. A literal zero divisor compiles without a diagnostic at both 85 and 2023; a warning would help but is not required.
reader.at-2023: mz_lit.cob compiles and prints Z1= 00000; mz_run.cob prints NO SIZE ERROR and zeros

refuter.evidence: Rule read whole (§1989:A.2.28.3 AR2 'The value of argument-2 must not be zero'); A.2.2 makes an out-of-range argument value a reference whose result is undefined, so no compile-time refusal and no particular runtime value is required. Runtime has four carriers (ModScaled, ModDec, ModExact, ModWide) and each returns ModZeroDivisor() on a zero divisor. Probe refute-1985-170/mod_ctx.cob at --std 85: the A.2.28.4 RV2 sign table (11,5)=1 (-11,5)=4 (11,-5)=-4 (-11,-5)=-1 on DISPLAY/COMP items, 18-digit MOD(-999999999999999999 100000000000000007)=71 and MOD(BIG -7)=0, MOD inside a division (1.3333) and as SQRT argument (2.0000), in an IF relation (Y) all match; zero divisor from a COMP-3 item and a literal 0 in COMPUTE, inside a division, inside SQRT, in an IF and with ON SIZE ERROR all yield 0 and execution continues (Z1..Z5, END). Undefined result admits that. cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.28.3 AR2  (2.28.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR2'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.2  (2.2 ARGUMENTS**)  the text is in the clause; it lies in AR4' [then the result of such a reference is undefined].
